subject: Day 14: first growth spurt; EPDS screening; open the 529
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 14. The first common growth spurt opens this week. Expect 24-48 hours of unusually frequent feeding (cluster feeding), then a reset. Anoushka's milk supply, if breastfeeding, calibrates to demand during this window. Resist the urge to supplement reflexively, but do not ignore signs of insufficient transfer.

Action items
- Take the EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale) screening for Anoushka this week if her OB has not administered it. A score above 10 warrants a call to her OB or PCP; a score of 13 or higher traditionally distinguishes likely depression. ACOG Committee Opinion 757 on perinatal depression screening: https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/11/screening-for-perinatal-depression
- Open the 529 plan once Avi's SSN has arrived (typical mail timing is 2-4 weeks post-birth). Front-loading the early years compounds maximally: $25,000 contributed at birth, growing at 7% real returns, becomes about $96,000 by age 18. 529 plan overview on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/529_plan
- Verify the insurance enrollment for Avi has actually processed. Call the insurer; do not trust that the form went through. Insurance companies do not retroactively cover the 1-month well visit if enrollment lapsed.
- Apply for paternity leave if not already on it. Coordinate with employer HR and California Paid Family Leave (up to 8 weeks). California EDD reference: https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/
- Reorder postpartum supplies that are running low. Anoushka is still in lochia rubra-to-serosa transition; pad supply matters.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cluster feeding for 24-48 hours, fussiness in the evenings, increased need to be held. Normal during the spurt.
- [low concern] Baby acne (neonatal cephalic pustulosis) peaking around week 3-4; resolves on its own.
- [monitor] Baby blues in Anoushka persisting beyond week 2. About 50-80% of mothers experience baby blues; resolution by 2 weeks postpartum is typical. Persistence escalates the concern toward postpartum depression. CDC overview: https://www.cdc.gov/reproductive-health/depression/index.html
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting after most feeds with weight stagnation (pyloric stenosis: typically male, first-born, presents weeks 3-6, surgical correction).
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F in an infant under 90 days. Apnea (a breathing pause longer than 20 seconds, or any pause with a color change). Seizure activity. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Mirror play: hold Avi in front of a mirror for 30-60 seconds during an awake-alert window. He is not recognizing himself yet, but the face-tracking response is the active ingredient; face-perception circuitry is tuning. Sustained eye contact during feeds will also start appearing this week.

Upcoming
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt (cluster feeding 24-48h).
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smile typically emerges.
- Day 35-42: peak of the PURPLE crying curve at about 6 weeks corrected age.
- Day 42: Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit (clearance for exercise and intimacy usually granted here).

Further reading
- The Opposite of Spoiled by Ron Lieber — money conversations with kids, starting now: https://www.harpercollins.com/products/the-opposite-of-spoiled-ron-lieber
- Cribsheet by Emily Oster — evidence-driven choices through preschool: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/562146/cribsheet-by-emily-oster/
- Postpartum Support International — screening, resources, hotline: https://www.postpartum.net/
- SavingForCollege guide to 529 plans: https://www.savingforcollege.com/

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Calms when picked up or spoken to
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calms-with-soothing/complete

- Briefly lifts head during tummy time
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brief-head-lift/complete

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete
